description:
The Augustiner Museum in Freiburg im Breisgau occupies a former monastic church and associated buildings. Its collections connect medieval and Baroque art with nineteenth-century painting and regional cultural history.

Sculpture and stained glass from Freiburg Minster sit alongside woodcarving, paintings, goldsmiths’ work and tapestries. The convent building broadens the museum’s account of the city and the surrounding Black Forest region.

description:

Dresden and its artists form the central focus, including nineteenth-century art, work made in East Germany and contemporary practice. The collection also documents the city through views and landscapes.

description:
The Freies Deutsches Hochstift in Frankfurt preserves art, manuscripts, books and objects associated with Goethe’s era. Its art collections developed alongside the acquisition of Goethe’s birthplace in 1863.

Painting, sculpture, prints and drawings illuminate German culture from the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, with particular connections to Romanticism. The Goethe House and museum collections form related parts of the institution.

Art made in East Germany is an important strand, alongside international artistic developments. The Albertinum also presents sculpture, whose collection remains distinct from the painting gallery.

description:
The Old Masters Picture Gallery in Kassel occupies Schloss Wilhelmshöhe. Its collection covers European painting from the fourteenth to eighteenth centuries and grew substantially through the collecting of the Hessian landgraves.

Dutch and Flemish painting is a particular strength, alongside German, Italian, French and Spanish works. The collection connects courtly patronage with the development of a public art museum.

description:
Berlin’s Gemäldegalerie surveys European painting from the thirteenth to eighteenth centuries. Founded as a public institution in 1830, its collections are presented at the Kulturforum.

German, Italian and Netherlandish painting form major strengths, connecting medieval and Renaissance traditions with the Baroque and eighteenth century. Portraits, landscapes, interiors and religious subjects offer different paths through the collection.

The State Museum in Schwerin holds art ranging from Dutch painting to modern and contemporary work. Its collections include an important group of paintings by Jean-Baptiste Oudry and works associated with Marcel Duchamp.

Painting, sculpture and graphic art offer different routes through the museum’s holdings. These art galleries are distinct from the historic interiors of the nearby Schwerin Castle museum.

description:
The State Gallery in Augsburg’s Katharinenkirche preserves painting associated with the late medieval and early Renaissance schools of Augsburg and Swabia. Its history as a Bavarian branch gallery reaches back to the early nineteenth century.

The church is closed while structural issues are investigated and repaired, and its artworks have been placed in storage. The operator has not announced a reopening date.
